title: Crossplane rollback concierge — prioritized tenant recovery & hotpatch liaison
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a runnable playbook and lightweight orchestration helper (the "rollback concierge") for production model rollout regressions that impact a subset of tenants across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to give SRE/oncall and the escalation liaison a concise, deterministic set of actions to: 1) prioritize tenant recovery based on business impact, 2) contain regressions without noisy global rollbacks, 3) apply surgical hotpatches or staged rollbacks while preserving KV cache and tenant isolation guarantees, and 4) coordinate customer communication and follow-through.

Why this is different:
- Existing runbooks emphasize coarse rollback choreography. This document focuses on a concierge workflow for prioritized tenant recovery (fast lane for high-$$ tenants) and guidance for mixed-deployment constraints (Hosted + Dedicated + Private).
- Includes concrete commands, gating checks, and a communication template tailored for live-customer escalation.

Scope / out of scope:
- In scope: model rollout regressions (quality regressions, prompt-affecting changes), canary failures that leak into tenant traffic, cross-environment coordination (Hosted <> Dedicated <> Private), KV cache mismatch scenarios during rollbacks, and applying hotpatch binaries/weights.
- Out of scope: infra-level hardware failures, network outages, or database corruption unrelated to model variants.

Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Immediate triage (T+0–10m):
   - Confirm regression signal: open-alert + customer report + metric delta (latency or quality). Pull the +alert dashboard and last 30m sample.
   - Verify scope: run tenant-slice query to identify impacted tenant IDs and slices (tools: slice-inspect --since 30m --model MODEL_ID).
   - If number of affected tenants > 25% of traffic, escalate to Incident Lead and consider global pause. Otherwise proceed with concierge path.

2) Fast-lane tenant pinning (T+10–30m):
   - For top-tier tenants (predefined in billing-priority list), pin traffic to last-known-good model version via routing API: curl -X POST $ROUTE_API/pin -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_ID","model":"MODEL_ID@vX.Y"}'.
   - Confirm KV cache reconciliation: run kv-reconcile --tenant TENANT_ID --model MODEL_ID@vX.Y and validate prefix-hits > 90% baseline. Document any cache invalidations.

3) Surgical canary quarantine (T+30–60m):
   - For remaining affected tenants, apply quarantine: add tenant slices to quarantine-policy with gradual diversion to fallback variant. quarantine-cli add --slices SLICE_IDS --fallback MODEL_ID@fallback.
   - Activate rate-limiting bridge (circuit-breaker) to avoid thundering during rollback: rbctl set --slice SLICE_ID --qps=Q where Q tuned to safe throughput.

4) Hotpatch or rollback decision matrix (T+60–120m):
   - If root cause is config/decoding change and a small binary patch exists: attempt hotpatch (live weight swap) following hotpatch checklist. Run dry-run on dedicated-staging-slice first.
   - If root cause is model quality regression with no safe hotpatch: prepare progressive rollback plan. Plan must include: per-region routing statements, KV cache reconciliation steps, TTL for prefix cache, and fallback grooming.

5) Rollback choreography (if chosen):
   - Phased rollout: 1) pin high-priority tenants, 2) rollback 10% of traffic slice-by-slice, 3) monitor for 15m windows of quality metrics, 4) expand to 50% then 100% if stable. Use rollout-cli start --plan-file /tmp/rollback-plan.yaml.
   - Watchlists: token error rate, semantic eval metric (BLEU/ROUGE surrogate + custom prompt tests), latency P95.
   - KV cache reconciliation: follow kv-replay plan to ensure inference artifacts are consistent. If sticky KVs observed, run kv-expunge for affected shards and warm cache with prioritized prompts.

6) Customer communication & liaison tasks:
   - Draft immediate outbound using template (see links). Notify Customer Success + Account Exec when top-tier tenant pinned.
   - Maintain a single shared triage doc (confluence) and update with timeline and next steps every 30 minutes until stable.

7) Post-incident actions (within 72h):
   - Postmortem with per-tenant impact table, root-cause, and follow-up PRs. Create postmortem tasks in the rollout-resilience epic.
   - Update rollout gating: add additional preflight checks for that model family (structured-eval harness + tenant-sampled prompts).

Decision criteria checklist (yes/no items):
- Is impact limited to <25% of tenants? (yes -> concierge flow)
- Are there high-value tenants in the impacted set? (yes -> pin first)
- Can we produce a hotpatch within 2 hours that passes staging checks? (yes -> hotpatch trial)
- Is KV cache mismatch expected after rollback? (yes -> plan kv-reconcile)

Operational aids / commands: (examples)
- slice-inspect --since 30m --model MODEL_ID
- route-api pin --tenant TENANT_ID --model MODEL_ID@vX.Y
- kv-reconcile --tenant TENANT_ID --dry-run
- quarantine-cli add --slices SLICE_IDS --fallback MODEL_ID@fallback
- rollout-cli start --plan-file /tmp/rollback-plan.yaml

Communication templates (copyable):
- Slack escalation (to #prod-escalations): 
  @oncall 
  Incident: model QA regression detected on MODEL_ID affecting {N} tenants. High-priority tenants pinned to MODEL_ID@vX.Y. Working on quarantine and safe rollback plan. Current action: running kv-reconcile and staging hotpatch verification. Will update in 30m.

- Customer-facing email (CS template): 
  Subject: Service update — short-term mitigation for model quality issue
  Body: We detected degraded outputs for some requests and have pinned your traffic to a verified model to protect output quality. Our engineers are running targeted remediation and will provide an update within 60 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we are prioritizing your tenant for recovery.

Monitoring and acceptance gates:
- Primary metric: service-quality-score (SQS) derived from eval prompts — require return to within 2% of baseline for 30m post-action.
- Secondary metrics: token error rate < 0.1%, latency P95 within 20% of baseline, no increase in 5xxs.

Artifact links and glossaries are in the links field below.

Exit criteria for this ticket:
- Top-tier tenants restored to pre-incident behavior and pinned or rolled back as agreed;
- KV cache reconciliation completed for acted tenants;
- Communication sent and postmortem task created;
- Any follow-up automated gating created in model onboarding pipeline.
